memberdef.name: Bulk

para.verbatim:
embed:rst Overview +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
Applies the function object ``op`` to each index in the provided shape The algorithm is similar to `bulk <https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg21/docs/papers/2022/p2300r5.html#design-sender-adaptor-bulk>`_ from P2300.
- The return value of ``op``, if any, is ignored. - When ``d_temp_storage`` is ``nullptr``, no work is done and the required allocation size is returned in ``temp_storage_bytes``.
A Simple Example +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
The following code snippet demonstrates how to use Bulk to square each element in a device vector.

memberdef.name: ForEachCopyN

para.verbatim:
embed:rst Overview +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
Applies the function object ``op`` to each element in the range ``[first, first + num_items)``. Unlike the ``ForEachN`` algorithm, ``ForEachCopyN`` is allowed to invoke ``op`` on copies of the elements. This relaxation allows ``ForEachCopyN`` to vectorize loads.
- Allowed to invoke ``op`` on copies of the elements - The return value of ``op``, if any, is ignored. - When ``d_temp_storage`` is ``nullptr``, no work is done and the required allocation size is returned in ``temp_storage_bytes``.

para.verbatim:
embed:rst Overview +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
Iterate through a multi-dimensional extents into
- a single linear index that represents the current iteration - indices of each extent dimension
Then apply a function object to the results.
- The return value of ``op``, if any, is ignored.
**Note**: ``DeviceFor::ForEachInExtents`` supports integral index type up to 64-bits.
A Simple Example +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
The following code snippet demonstrates how to use ``ForEachInExtents`` to tabulate a 3D array with its coordinates.
.. literalinclude:: ../../../cub/test/catch2_test_device_for_each_in_extents_api.cu :language: c++ :dedent: :start-after: example-begin for-each-in-extents-op :end-before: example-end for-each-in-extents-op
